title: UnitedHealth Stock (UNH) Falls 10.2% on CMS Audit Proposal (Nov 18)
summary: UnitedHealth (UNH) fell 10.21% to $349.91 on Nov 18, 2026, as a CMS proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits weighed on health insurers.
body_markdown:
## Why UnitedHealth Stock Fell


The selling traces to a proposed rule from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), announced on November 16 by the Department of Health and Human Services, as reported by[Medical Daily](https://www.medicaldaily.com/cms-crush-rule-medicare-advantage-audits-481315) . According to the[CMS proposed rule](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-23461.pdf) (CMS-6098-P), the agency plans to apply extrapolation to Medicare Advantage risk adjustment data validation (RADV) audits for payment year 2018 forward and to require insurers to remit improper payments found in those audits. CMS estimates extrapolated recoveries of approximately $9 billion per audit year, beginning with the 2018 audits.


On Wednesday, health care stocks came under considerable pressure, with Humana falling nearly 13% alongside UnitedHealth, according to[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/18/stock-market-today-nov-18-s-and-p-500-breaks-key-support-as-fed-minutes-signal-more-rate-hikes-ahead/) . The outlet tied the sell-off to the federal proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits and recover improper payments dating back to 2018, which it said could expose insurers to substantial financial liabilities. The move extended the[5.4% decline in UnitedHealth shares on November 17](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/unitedhealth-unh-stock-news-november-18-2026/) .


The broader CRUSH proposal targets fraud, waste and abuse in Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP and the Marketplace, and HHS projects it would save nearly $90 billion in federal spending over 10 years, per Medical Daily.


## UNH Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- The measure is a proposed rule, not a final one, and the public can comment until January 19, 2027, per Medical Daily.
- CMS says it is reissuing the extrapolation provisions because a US District Court for the Northern District of Texas vacated similar provisions of a 2023 CMS final rule for procedural reasons, so the approach has been set aside in court once before.
- The roughly $9 billion per audit year is CMS's estimate for the Medicare Advantage industry as a whole, not a figure specific to UnitedHealth.


### Risks


- The proposal would extrapolate audit findings from payment year 2018 forward and require insurers to remit improper payments, which could reach several past payment years if it is finalized as proposed.
- CMS says it decided not to apply a fee-for-service (FFS) adjuster when calculating RADV overpayments, according to the proposed rule.
- The selling reached beyond UnitedHealth, with Humana down nearly 13% in the same session, per The Motley Fool.
